_balance: Balanced so every mission pays about the same per study session as Explore (about 60-90 on top of the base session pay), with rarer or harder ones up to about 2-3x, and passive income (posts, crew, deliveries) smaller than one Explore trip. Meant for a long game.
_help: Solarist economy. Every resource income and price in the game. Edit the numbers, save, reload the page. Delete a line (or the whole file) to fall back to the built-in default. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored.
_incomeMultiplier: Every resource payout below (except the Distress Run) is multiplied by this. 1 = as written, 1.5 = 50% more.

session._note: Each finished study session pays perStudyMinute x session length (at least minimum), plus eventBonus if a deep-space event happened, plus rarityBonus for the world found on an Explore trip.

_researchCost: Every research's Knowledge-point price is its base cost x this (rounded to 5). 1 = the original prices.
_engineBonusPerLevel: Engine module: session pay x (1 + this x (level - 1)).
_fight: Extra resources for driving outlaws off a world (random between min and max).
_fullCycle: Paid when a Full Cycle (no skipping) ends: base + perHullLevel x (Hull level - 1).
_bountyMultiplier: Scales every bounty reward when the bounty is created.
_encounter: The arrival roll: every new world has this chance (0.3 = 3 in 10) of one visitor, and the weights pick which one (a world never gets two). meeting = a chance meeting that pays a little, trade = Trade Station, outlaw = an outlaw gang holds the world, derelict = a derelict ship to salvage, station = Interplanetary Station. postal = a Postal office with delivery jobs, cassini = a Cassini Federation Post with a Most Wanted poster.
_encounters: Chance meetings: scale multiplies every meeting's own min-max pay, rareWorldMultiplier applies on Rare and Legendary worlds.
_investigate: Investigate (worlds with an anomaly): each study session adds between min and max progress (0.25 = 25%). When it reaches 100%: pay resources, knowledge Knowledge points, a Codex entry and an Anomalies find.
_hyperdrive: Hyperdrive charges: the most you can hold (one study session of Charge makes one; one jump to any visited world uses one). nodeRefund = resources paid back once for each old Hyperdrive Node.
_postal: Postal offices (an arrival visitor): how many jobs one offers, how many you can carry at once, and the share of pay given back once for a job that was cancelled when daily deliveries ended.
_cassini: Cassini Federation Posts hand out Most Wanted posters. While you carry one, each new world has base chance of a sighting, plus perTrip for every trip without one, up to cap. A sighting opens a 3-session Manhunt there: legPay resources for each of the first two parts, then the bounty (quests bossBase + bossPerCatch).
_expedition: Planet expeditions (3 parts per world). pay = resources per part (a risky part pays boldPay x that), finale = extra on the last part, findSafe / findBold = chance of a collectible on a safe / risky part (the finale always finds one), poiSellBonus = how much each Point of Interest adds to a world's sale price (0.08 = 8%), salvage = resources for salvaging a derelict.
_trade: Travelers' Posts pay perFacilityLevel per facility level (all posts together) every study session, up to cap.

sell._note: Selling a world: the sum of everything that applies to it. earthLike is added at earthLikeAt% habitability or more.

_distressRun: Daily Distress Run payout: base + 0..random (not affected by incomeMultiplier). bonusMin-bonusMax is the extra-resources random bonus.
_tradeStation: Trade Stations (how often: see encounter): what its collectibles cost (each varies by up to 15%), and the share of that price it pays for your spares (before incomeMultiplier).
_moduleCost: Ship module upgrade price: base x growth ^ (current level - 1). maxLevel is each module's top level (past it the effect would stop growing anyway).
_roomCost: Upgrading a ship room to level L costs base x growth ^ (L - 1). The first level is built with a study session instead.
_crewCost: Hiring costs base + perCrew x crew already aboard.
_shipStyleCost: Buying a hull paint color (once; switching between owned ones is free). design is only used to refund old ship designs.
_decorCost: Ship decorations by price tier (t1 cheapest .. t4 fanciest). station = price of a station-only decoration at an Interplanetary Station.
_story: The Meridian story: pay for each chapter part, a bonus for finishing a chapter, and the reward at the very end.
_levels: Captain and Knowledge Levels: going from level L to L+1 needs base + perLevel x L + perLevelSquared x L x L points. Bigger perLevelSquared = steeper late game. The old curve was base 40, perLevel 6, perLevelSquared 0.
_ratingRanks: Rating needed for each rank, in order: Stowaway, Deckhand, Drifter, Wayfarer, Surveyor, Pathfinder, Voyager, Star Captain, Trailblazer, Living Legend, Myth of the Void. The old values were 0, 300, 1000, 2500, 5000, 9000, 15000, 25000, 40000, 65000, 100000.
_station: Interplanetary Station (how often: see encounter): the upgrade discount and sell bonus while you stay at its world, its shop prices, and maxShifts = how many shifts you can work per station.
_coordChips: Coordinator Panel chips: how many you start with, the price of the first one you buy (each next one costs growth x more), and the most you can own.
_facilitySlots: How many facilities fit at one Travelers' Post, plus extra slots once it grows into a Town (1,000 settlers). You can buy more land up to max slots: the first costs buyBase, each next one buyGrowth x more.
_quests: deliveryViaJump: pay multiplier when you drop a delivery off at a world you jumped to with the hyperdrive. delivery: the base pay of an Interstellar Delivery (a job that fits 1 world in N pays about N^0.9 times this, up to 45x). Guild contract: the resource and Knowledge-point choices. Most Wanted: base payout plus bossPerCatch for every boss caught before.
_facilityCost: Facility upgrade price to reach level L: base x growth ^ (L - 2). maxLevel is the highest level.
